clue.text: High wind ravaged first-century Ceylon

indicators.note: something ravaged has been wrecked and thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged
first asks for only the opening letter of the word it is attached to

parts.note: the opening letter of century
taken as written; the old name of Sri Lanka

explanation.surface: A storm wrecked Ceylon in the first century AD.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first-century' reads as a date, but it means just the first letter of century, which joins the island's name in the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: A cyclone is a violent rotating storm, a classic example of very strong wind.

clue.text: Head of Finance

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the top part of a column, or a head city
second meaning: money available for investment

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a job title, Head of Finance; split it at 'of' into two separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital is the crowning top section of a pillar, and also the stock of money a business works with.

clue.text: Museum keeper introduces artist in engraved gold

indicators.note: to be introduces into something is to be put inside it, so the artist goes within the engraving word

parts.note: to engrave is to cut lines into a surface
RA, Royal Academician, a standard abbreviation for an artist
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A museum official brings an artist's work set in engraved gold into the collection.
explanation.walkthrough: Gold is OR in heraldry, a convention setters use constantly; the artist is the usual Royal Academician.
explanation.definitionFit: A curator is the person in charge of a museum or gallery collection, its keeper.

clue.text: Last letter is partly to Megan

indicators.note: partly means only a portion of the following words is used, a run of letters spanning them

parts.note: the run of letters across the end of to and the start of Megan

explanation.surface: The final letter of a correspondence is addressed in part to Megan.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the final character of the Greek alphabet, hence the last letter.

clue.text: Texts emir about dangerous radical

indicators.note: about suggests turning around or moving here and there, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; an emir is a Muslim ruler

explanation.surface: A ruler sends messages about a dangerous radical.
explanation.definitionFit: An extremist holds radical views and may support violent means, a dangerous radical.

clue.text: Fictional detective's chasing heartless rogue to expose guilt

indicators.note: something chasing comes behind, so the detective sits after the other piece
heartless removes the middle of the word, keeping only its two ends

parts.note: the first and last letters of rogue
Inspector Morse, Colin Dexter's Oxford detective

explanation.surface: A TV detective pursues a scoundrel to make him reveal his guilty conscience.
explanation.definitionFit: Remorse is deep regret for wrongdoing, the feeling of guilt.

clue.text: Right to get life after setting off a gun

parts.note: R is the standard abbreviation for right

indicators.note: setting off suggests an explosion, which scatters the word into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sentenced to life after setting off a gun gets what they deserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setting off a gun' paints a shooting, but setting off belongs to life, and 'a gun' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A rifle is a long-barrelled firearm, one particular kind of gun.

clue.text: Zoo in Maine keeps old horse down by the lake

indicators.note: in a down entry, something down by another sits below it, so it comes after

parts.note: ME is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Maine
a nag is an old or worn-out horse
Lake Erie, one of the Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A Maine zoo houses an old horse down by the lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A menagerie is a collection of wild animals kept for show, an old word for a zoo.

clue.text: Nastier variety of wine

indicators.note: a variety is a different version or form, so the letters take on another arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A rather unpleasant kind of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that retsina, flavoured with pine resin, is a wine many find nasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin.

clue.text: Scramble to point inside eastern burial chamber

indicators.note: inside places the compass point within the following words

parts.note: E for east, eastern
N, north, a point of the compass
a crypt is an underground vault for burials

explanation.surface: An instruction to clamber to a spot inside an eastern tomb.
explanation.walkthrough: The point goes inside, between eastern and the burial chamber.
explanation.definitionFit: To encrypt a message is to scramble it into code so outsiders cannot read it.

clue.text: English parfait couldn't be better

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the English translation of the French word parfait

explanation.walkthrough: Parfait looks like the dessert, but here it is just French for a word you must give in English.
explanation.definitionFit: Something flawless and ideal is beyond improvement; parfait in French carries exactly that sense.

clue.text: Devotee of blow's a jerk

parts.note: to fan is to blow air on something
taken as written
a tic is an involuntary twitch or jerk

explanation.surface: A fan of fisticuffs is a bit of a jerk.
explanation.definitionFit: A fanatic is an extremely keen enthusiast, a devotee of some cause or pursuit.

clue.text: French heads are holding a private conversation

indicators.note: something holding another keeps it inside, so the heads wrap around the next letter

parts.note: tete is French for head, so two heads give it twice
taken as written

explanation.surface: French leaders are having a private chat.
explanation.walkthrough: The A goes between the two French heads.
explanation.definitionFit: A tete-a-tete, literally head-to-head, is an intimate talk between two people.

clue.text: Stern on leading yacht's really dirty

parts.note: stern and grim both mean severe

indicators.note: leading points to the letter at the front of the word it qualifies

parts.note: the opening letter of yacht

explanation.surface: The back end of the lead yacht is filthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stern' looks like the rear of a boat, which suits the yacht, but it is the adjective meaning severe.
explanation.definitionFit: Grimy means covered in ingrained grime, so very dirty.

clue.text: Student has taken to old city I would find garish

parts.note: L for learner, a student driver
Ur, the ancient Sumerian city
I'd is the contraction of I would

explanation.surface: A student who has taken up an ancient city as a subject finds it tasteless.
explanation.definitionFit: Lurid colours are unnaturally vivid and glaring, the same as garish.

clue.text: Media star taking break to adapt for the theatre

indicators.note: taking a break breaks the words apart, and the pieces are reassembled differently

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A celebrity takes time off to turn something into a stage play.
explanation.definitionFit: To dramatise a story is to rewrite it as a play for performance.

clue.text: Bring in worker who's valued

parts.note: to import goods is to bring them in from abroad
the worker ant, a standard crossword worker

explanation.surface: An employer recruits a staff member who is highly prized.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone important is of great significance, someone much valued.

clue.text: Product presentation by company's becoming dated

parts.note: a pack is a group or company of animals or people
growing old, the US-style spelling of ageing

explanation.surface: A firm's way of displaying its goods is looking old-fashioned.
explanation.definitionFit: Packaging is the wrapping and design in which goods are presented for sale.

clue.text: Mocking actors wearing Indian dress at club

indicators.note: someone wearing a garment is inside it, so the actors go within the dress

parts.note: a sari is the draped garment worn by many Indian women
the cast is the set of actors in a production
C for clubs, the card suit

explanation.surface: Performers dressed in saris at a club are being ridiculed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club' looks like a nightclub venue, but it is the card suit, supplying a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarcastic remarks use irony to scorn or ridicule, so they are mocking.

clue.text: Fruit from somewhere in Japan

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a small loose-skinned citrus fruit
second meaning: a former province in southern Kyushu

explanation.walkthrough: The fruit really is named after the Japanese province, so the surface is literally true.
explanation.definitionFit: The satsuma mandarin takes its name from the old Japanese province where it was cultivated.

clue.text: Refuse to criticise

definitions.meaning: first meaning: waste, garbage (the noun, stressed on the first syllable)
second meaning: to dismiss scornfully as worthless

explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse to criticise' reads as declining to find fault, but refuse is the noun for waste; British 'rubbish' as a verb means to pan.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbish is British for household waste, and to rubbish something is to disparage it.

clue.text: Refuse right away to get thrown out

definitions.note: a past participle standing for the verb meaning throw out

indicators.note: away tells you to remove the letter for right from the word

parts.note: to refuse something is to reject it
R for right, the letter taken out

explanation.surface: Turn something down at once and you get chucked out.
explanation.walkthrough: Refuse is a verb this time, unlike in 18 Down; drop R from REJECT.
explanation.definitionFit: To eject someone is to expel them forcibly, to throw them out.

clue.text: Implicate bishop in Rome playing with the Italian following

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the Italian word is placed at the end
playing suggests moving freely about, so the letters change places

parts.note: B is the chess notation for bishop
taken as written
il is Italian for the

explanation.surface: A bishop is caught up in some scheme in Rome involving an Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: To embroil someone is to drag them into a conflict, to implicate them in it.

clue.text: Rolls taken from the Yorkshire diners, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said out loud, so the sound counts rather than the spelling

parts.note: Yorkshire dialect shortens the to t', and diners are eaters

explanation.surface: Bread rolls are being taken by Yorkshire people eating out.
explanation.walkthrough: Rolls looks like bread but is a verb, rocking unsteadily. In Yorkshire speech 'the' is clipped to t', as in 'on t'moor'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that teeters sways or rocks unsteadily, as a ship rolls.

clue.text: Brought back first-class piece of shin

indicators.note: something brought back returns the way it came, so the letters run from right to left

parts.note: A1 means first-class, with the 1 standing as the letter I
a bit is a piece

explanation.surface: Someone returned a top-quality piece of shin, perhaps from the butcher.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is a common phrase for first-rate, and setters let the digit 1 serve as I.
explanation.definitionFit: The tibia is the shinbone, the larger bone of the lower leg.

clue.text: Easily persuaded to take short way to bar

indicators.note: short means cut off before the end, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a track is a path or way
to table a proposal, in American usage, is to shelve it, barring its discussion

explanation.surface: Someone is readily talked into a shortcut to the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: The bar of the surface is a pub, but here it is a verb: in American usage, tabling a motion sets it aside. The link 'to take' is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: A tractable person is docile and manageable, readily led or persuaded.

clue.text: Your old style repast is lacking a little herb

parts.note: thy is the archaic form of your

indicators.note: is lacking means some letters are missing from the meal word

parts.note: a repast is a meal
A as written and L, an abbreviation for little; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned meal of yours is missing a pinch of herbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Thyme is an aromatic garden herb used in cooking.

clue.text: One accepting offer as Speaker's no Liberal

indicators.note: no means without, so the letter for Liberal is taken out

parts.note: a speaker is one who talks
L, the abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: A politician accepts a deal, given the Commons Speaker isn't a Liberal.
explanation.definitionFit: A taker is someone who accepts what is offered, as in 'any takers?'.

clue.text: Usefulness of electricity, say?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the quality of being useful
second meaning: a public service such as power, gas or water

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as asking how useful electricity is; 'say' flags that electricity is just one example of the second meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Utility means usefulness, and a utility is also a public service like electricity supply.

clue.text: Heard aircraftman's a bit annoying

indicators.note: heard means we take the sound of the following word, not its spelling

parts.note: erk is RAF slang for a lowest-rank aircraftman
some means a bit, a certain amount

explanation.surface: An airman was overheard being slightly irritating.
explanation.walkthrough: An erk is British forces slang for an aircraftman, the lowest RAF rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Something irksome is tiresome and irritating, hence annoying.

clue.text: I've worked in agony to win

indicators.note: in places the reworked letters inside the word for agony

parts.note: an ache is a pain

indicators.note: worked means shaped or kneaded, so the letters are reformed

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: An athlete says they worked through great pain to triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I've worked' reads as someone describing their effort, but worked only rearranges the contraction before it.
explanation.definitionFit: To achieve something is to succeed in gaining it, to win it.

clue.text: Corsets made ridges around top of leg!

indicators.note: around means the reworked letters encircle the single letter
made suggests something constructed anew, so the letters are formed into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: top of, in an across clue, picks out the very first letter of the next word

parts.note: the opening letter of leg

explanation.surface: Tight undergarments left welts around the thigh.
explanation.walkthrough: L sits inside GIRD-ES.
explanation.definitionFit: A girdle is a close-fitting elastic undergarment, a type of corset.
